CREATE TABLE region_board (
  customer_id integer PRIMARY KEY,
  region text,
  changed_at timestamptz NOT NULL
);
INSERT INTO region_board (customer_id, region, changed_at) VALUES
  (1, 'North', '2025-12-28T00:00:00Z'),
  (4, 'Central', '2025-12-28T00:00:00Z');
MERGE INTO region_board AS b
USING (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.customer_id) r.customer_id, r.region, r.changed_at
  FROM staging_customer_regions AS r
  JOIN customers AS c ON c.id = r.customer_id
  ORDER BY r.customer_id, r.changed_at DESC NULLS LAST
) AS f
ON b.customer_id = f.customer_id
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET region = f.region, changed_at = f.changed_at
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY TARGET THEN INSERT (customer_id, region, changed_at) VALUES (f.customer_id, f.region, f.changed_at)
WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE;

ambiguities: "Delete a board row whose customer the feed does not report": I read this as absent from the feed altogether. Each reported known customer has exactly one newest change here, so the result is the same under the other reading.
The text does not say whether a feed change older than the board row's changed_at should be ignored. Every feed change is newer than the seeded 2025-12-28 rows, so this did not change the answer.
The text gives no foreign key for region_board. I added none. The unknown customer is filtered by the join, so this does not affect the state.
NULL region or changed_at in the feed is not described. No dataset has NULL feed rows, so this did not change the answer.
notes: Ran on sample, nulls and nulltext: all three give the same 3 rows. This ticket does not run twice, so no second run. Own probes: NULL changed_at gives 23502, repeated customer 2 gives 23505. The MERGE needed WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE, which PostgreSQL 18.6 accepted.
